subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Who was the last ruling Nizam of the princely state of Hyderabad who resisted accession to the Indian Union in 1947-48?
options: A) Mir Osman Ali Khan
B) Maharaja Hari Singh
C) Nawab Hamidullah Khan
D) Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh
questions.explanation: Mir Osman Ali Khan (Asaf Jah VII) was the Nizam of Hyderabad whose reluctance to merge with India led to Operation Polo in September 1948.

questions.question: Which visionary socialist leader coined the concept of 'Non-Congressism' (Gair-Congressvad) to forge anti-Congress electoral alliances in the 1960s?
options: A) Acharya Narendra Deva
B) Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia
C) Jayaprakash Narayan
D) Ashoka Mehta
questions.explanation: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia formulated the strategy of 'Non-Congressism' to unite ideologically divergent opposition parties to defeat Congress in 1967.

questions.question: The nationwide rural development programme initiated in 1970 to create a nationwide milk grid is popularly known as:
options: A) Operation Blue Star
B) Operation Green Harvest
C) Operation Flood (White Revolution)
D) Operation Evergreen
questions.explanation: Operation Flood, launched by the National Dairy Development Board in 1970, transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer.

questions.question: The 1965 war between India and Pakistan was brought to a diplomatic conclusion through which declaration signed in Soviet Uzbekistan in January 1966?
options: A) Simla Agreement
B) Lahore Declaration
C) Agra Accord
D) Tashkent Declaration
questions.explanation: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan.

questions.question: Mikhail Gorbachev sought to reform the Soviet political and economic system through two famous Russian policies: Glasnost (openness) and:
options: A) Perestroika (restructuring)
B) Apparatchik
C) Kolkhoz
D) Gosplan
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev's dual policies were 'Glasnost' (political transparency/openness) and 'Perestroika' (economic and structural rebuilding).

questions.question: The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) appointed by the Union Government under Justice Fazal Ali submitted its comprehensive report in:
options: A) August 1947
B) September 1955
C) January 1950
D) December 1962
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in December 1953 and submitted its recommendations in September 1955, paving the way for the 1956 Act.

questions.question: In October 1956, shortly before his death, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led a historic mass conversion of nearly half a million followers to Buddhism in:
options: A) Mumbai, Maharashtra
B) Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
C) Nagpur, Maharashtra
D) Patna, Bihar
questions.explanation: On 14 October 1956, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and his followers formally embraced Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur, renouncing the Hindu caste system.

questions.question: The 'Kerala Model' of development is internationally celebrated because it achieved:
options: A) Massive heavy industrial steel manufacturing exceeding all other states
B) The total elimination of public healthcare in favor of commercial private hospitals
C) Complete exemption of multinational corporate enterprises from state taxation
D) High literacy, low infant mortality, high life expectancy, and land reforms despite relatively low per capita industrial income
questions.explanation: The Kerala Model refers to the state's remarkable human development indicators (health, education, longevity) achieved through public investment and social reforms despite modest economic growth.

questions.question: The October 1962 Sino-Indian border war was fought simultaneously across two widely separated geographical fronts:
options: A) The North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA, now Arunachal Pradesh) and the Aksai Chin region of Ladakh
B) The Rann of Kutch and the Thar Desert
C) Sikkim and the Andaman Islands
D) Kashmir Valley and the Punjab plains
questions.explanation: Chinese troops launched coordinated simultaneous offensives in the eastern sector (NEFA/Arunachal Pradesh) and the western sector (Aksai Chin/Ladakh) in October 1962.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia justified the strategy of 'Non-Congressism' by arguing that:
options: A) Parliamentary democracy was obsolete and must be replaced by a military dictatorship.
B) Congress rule was anti-people and undemocratic; hence opposition parties needed to unite across ideological lines to restore power to the poor.
C) All private agricultural properties should be seized by the central government immediately.
D) India should unconditionally merge its foreign policy into the Warsaw Pact.
questions.explanation: Lohia argued that Congress dominance concentrated power in an oligarchic elite, and non-Congressism was essential to restore popular democracy.

questions.question: During the Emergency of 1975-77, leading national newspapers such as The Indian Express and The Statesman protested against government pre-censorship by:
options: A) Publishing only cartoons and horoscope columns
B) Printing entirely in Russian and Chinese alphabets
C) Leaving their editorial columns completely blank
D) Closing down their printing presses permanently
questions.explanation: Newspapers like The Indian Express and The Statesman left their editorial spaces blank to silently protest censorship rules imposed under Emergency regulations.

questions.question: Less than a month after signing the historic Punjab Accord with Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in July 1985, Akali leader Sant Harchand Singh Longowal was:
options: A) Elected unopposed as Chief Minister of Punjab
B) Appointed as Governor of Jammu & Kashmir
C) Exiled to the United Kingdom by the Union government
D) Assassinated by Sikh militants who opposed the accord
questions.explanation: Sant Harchand Singh Longowal was gunned down by Sikh extremists at a gurdwara in Sherpur on 20 August 1985, within a month of signing the accord.

questions.question: What was the iconic ecological slogan popularized by women activists during the Chipko movement in the 1970s?
options: A) 'What do the forests bear? Soil, water and pure air. Soil, water and pure air are the basis of life.'
B) 'Industrial growth is national strength; fell trees to build factories.'
C) 'One nation, one crop, one global market.'
D) 'Axe the old pines to plant commercial eucalyptus.'
questions.explanation: The women of the Chipko movement countered commercial foresters by articulating the foundational ecological truth: 'Soil, water and pure air are the basis of life.'

questions.question: In April 1997, when the Congress withdrew support from H.D. Deve Gowda, who was chosen as the consensus candidate of the United Front to become Prime Minister?
options: A) Mulayam Singh Yadav
B) I.K. Gujral
C) Lalu Prasad Yadav
D) P.A. Sangma
questions.explanation: Inder Kumar Gujral was sworn in as Prime Minister in April 1997, leading the United Front until Congress withdrew support again in November 1997.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment act enacted in January 2019 provided up to 10% reservation in educational institutions and civil posts for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)?
options: A) 100th Constitutional Amendment Act
B) 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act
C) 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act
D) 104th Constitutional Amendment Act
questions.explanation: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019 amended Articles 15 and 16, enabling a 10% quota for Economically Weaker Sections of citizens not covered under SC/ST/OBC quotas.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The tense Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 occurred almost simultaneously with which major regional war in Asia?
options: A) The Vietnam War offensive at Tet
B) The Korean War armistice
C) The Indo-Pakistani War over Bangladesh
D) The Sino-Indian Border War
questions.explanation: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962) preoccupied both superpowers, coinciding exactly with China's military offensive across India's borders on 20 October 1962.

questions.question: The implementation of Shock Therapy in Russia caused which severe macroeconomic catastrophe in the early 1990s?
options: A) The value of the Russian Ruble collapsed dramatically and hyperinflation wiped out the life savings of ordinary citizens.
B) Russia accumulated the world's largest budget surplus within six months.
C) The price of bread and consumer goods fell to near-zero levels.
D) All foreign multinational corporations were permanently expelled from Russia.
questions.explanation: With sudden price decontrol and withdrawal of subsidies under Shock Therapy, the ruble crashed, inflation skyrocketed into hundreds of percent, and collective savings evaporated.

questions.question: The 1991 First Gulf War established the emergence of US hegemony primarily by demonstrating:
options: A) The complete disappearance of all sovereign boundaries in the Middle East
B) The immense technological qualitative gap between the US military and the rest of the world
C) The total superiority of infantry guerrilla tactics over electronic guidance
D) The permanent retirement of all naval carrier fleets worldwide
questions.explanation: Desert Storm demonstrated American supremacy in precision guidance, satellite intelligence, stealth aircraft, and night vision, leaving Iraqi forces completely outmatched.

questions.question: In 2007, ASEAN leaders decided to accelerate the target year for establishing the ASEAN Community across its three pillars from 2020 to:
questions.explanation: At the 12th ASEAN Summit in Cebu in January 2007, leaders signed a declaration accelerating the realization of the ASEAN Community to 31 December 2015.

questions.question: The 'Four Modernizations' framework adopted by China in 1978 prioritized modernization in agriculture, industry, national defense, and:
options: A) Religious institutions
B) Constitutional jurisprudence
C) Traditional herbal medicine
D) Science and technology
questions.explanation: First proposed by Zhou Enlai and enacted by Deng Xiaoping, the Four Modernizations focused on Agriculture, Industry, National Defense, and Science & Technology.

questions.question: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement aimed to reduce customs duties on traded goods among member states to zero by:
questions.explanation: Signed in 2004, SAFTA envisioned lowering tariffs on traded goods to below 5% and ultimately towards zero across member nations by 2016.

questions.question: The G4 grouping, which mutually supports each other's bids for permanent seats on an expanded UN Security Council, comprises India, Brazil, Germany, and:
options: A) South Africa
B) Japan
C) Australia
D) Canada
questions.explanation: The Group of Four (G4) consists of India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan, four countries with major economic and geopolitical weight campaigning for permanent UNSC representation.

questions.question: In traditional military security analysis, 'Deterrence' is differentiated from 'Defense' because Deterrence seeks to:
options: A) Surrender immediately without firing a shot to avoid civilian casualties.
B) Sign unilateral treaties renouncing the sovereign right to maintain an army.
C) Prevent war from occurring by threatening unacceptable retaliation, whereas Defense aims to limit damage or halt an attack once war begins.
D) Deploy biological weapons along civilian border communities in peacetime.
questions.explanation: Deterrence prevents war by convincing the enemy that the cost of attack outweighs benefits; defense is the actual fighting capability deployed if deterrence breaks down.

questions.question: Alongside the Climate Change convention (UNFCCC), which other legally binding multilateral treaty was opened for signature at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
options: A) Montreal Protocol on CFCs
B) Kyoto Protocol on Emissions
C) Antarctic Treaty on Science
D) Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
questions.explanation: The Earth Summit produced two legally binding multilateral agreements: the UNFCCC and the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), alongside Agenda 21.

questions.question: The World Social Forum (WSF), embodying transnational resistance against corporate globalization, operates under the rallying slogan:
options: A) 'Another World is Possible'
B) 'There Is No Alternative (TINA)'
C) 'Free Trade for All Nations'
D) 'Global Corporations Unite'
questions.explanation: 'Another World is Possible' is the defining slogan of the World Social Forum, expressing hope for a humane, ecological, and democratic world beyond neoliberal capitalism.

questions.question: The standard Instrument of Accession signed by rulers of princely states in 1947 surrendered authority to the Dominion of India exclusively over which three subjects?
options: A) Finance, Agriculture, and Police
B) Defense, External Affairs, and Communications
C) Education, Health, and Land Revenue
D) Mining, Railways, and Religious Endowments
questions.explanation: The Instrument of Accession preserved internal autonomy for the princely states while transferring jurisdiction over Defense, External Affairs, and Communications to the central government.

questions.sub_topic: Voting Technology in First General Elections
questions.question: During the first general elections in 1951-52, how was secret voting conducted for an electorate where over 85% of citizens were illiterate?
options: A) Voters publicly announced their preference to presiding officers who recorded them in a register.
B) Voters punched holes into automated electronic voting machines imported from Britain.
C) Each polling booth had separate steel ballot boxes for each candidate, painted with the candidate's unique election symbol, into which voters dropped a blank ballot paper.
D) Voters cast physical bronze tokens into a single common urn marked with the national emblem.
questions.explanation: Over 2 million steel ballot boxes were manufactured; each candidate was allotted a dedicated box bearing their symbol inside a private screened compartment.

questions.question: During the Second Five Year Plan, India established three major public sector steel plants in collaboration with foreign governments. Which of the following correctly matches the plant with its foreign collaborator?
options: A) Bhilai — United States; Rourkela — United Kingdom; Durgapur — Soviet Union
B) Bhilai — West Germany; Rourkela — France; Durgapur — Japan
C) Bhilai — Soviet Union; Rourkela — United States; Durgapur — Canada
D) Bhilai — Soviet Union; Rourkela — West Germany; Durgapur — United Kingdom
questions.explanation: Bhilai (Madhya Pradesh/Chhattisgarh) was built with USSR support; Rourkela (Odisha) with German firms Krupp and Demag; Durgapur (West Bengal) with a British consortium.

questions.question: In August 1965, Pakistan's military leadership launched 'Operation Gibraltar', which directly precipitated the full-scale 1965 war. What was the objective of Operation Gibraltar?
options: A) Infiltrating thousands of trained Pakistani soldiers disguised as local Kashmiri civilians across the Ceasefire Line to incite an armed rebellion against India.
B) Conducting a naval amphibious assault to capture the port of Mumbai.
C) Launching an airborne paratrooper assault on the nuclear reactor at Trombay.
D) Establishing permanent artillery bunkers in the Rann of Kutch salt flats.
questions.explanation: Operation Gibraltar aimed to spark a popular uprising in Jammu and Kashmir by infiltrating commando units; local Kashmiris alerted Indian forces, leading India to cross the international border in Punjab.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The 1969 presidential election remains the only election in Indian history decided on the counting of second-preference votes. Who emerged victorious as an independent candidate?
options: A) Dr. Zakir Husain, defeating C. Rajagopalachari
B) V.V. Giri, defeating official Congress candidate Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
C) Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, defeating Morarji Desai
D) K.R. Narayanan, defeating T.N. Seshan
questions.explanation: V.V. Giri polled 420,077 value votes against Sanjiva Reddy's 405,427 after second preferences were counted, cementing Indira Gandhi's dominance over the Syndicate.

questions.question: During the 1975-77 Emergency, thousands of political leaders, journalists, and activists were arrested without trial under which draconian preventive detention statute?
options: A) Prevention of Terrorism Act (POTA)
B) Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Act (TADA)
C) Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA)
D) Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA)
questions.explanation: MISA was aggressively amended during the Emergency to permit indefinite preventive detention of political opponents without disclosing grounds of arrest or judicial review.

questions.sub_topic: Shillong Accord and Genesis of NSCN
questions.question: The 1975 Shillong Accord between the Government of India and underground Naga leaders led to a bitter split in the Naga movement because:
options: A) The accord mandated the immediate dissolution of Nagaland's state assembly.
B) All underground fighters were immediately recruited into the Indian Navy.
C) The United Nations rejected the treaty as a violation of international maritime law.
D) Isak Chishi Swu, Thuingaleng Muivah, and S.S. Khaplang rejected the surrender of arms and subsequently founded the National Socialist Council of Nagaland (NSCN) in 1980.
questions.explanation: Radical Naga leaders viewed the Shillong Accord as a betrayal, repudiated it from their base in Myanmar, and formed the NSCN in 1980 to continue the armed struggle for a sovereign Nagalim.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Kisan Union's massive siege of Meerut in January 1988 highlighted peasant demands centered on:
options: A) Higher government procurement prices for sugarcane and wheat, subsidised electricity, and waiver of agricultural debt arrears
B) The complete nationalisation of all arable land under state-run cooperative farms
C) The abolition of all private seed markets and replacement by Soviet state trusts
D) The introduction of high income tax on all agricultural landlords
questions.explanation: The BKU's agitations were characterized by economic demands: higher MSP, affordable electricity tariffs, debt relief, and removal of interstate trade bans on sugarcane.

questions.question: In Indira Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), while upholding 27% OBC quotas, the Supreme Court placed which crucial constitutional ceiling on reservations?
options: A) No state could offer reservations exceeding 10% under any circumstance.
B) Total reservation quota in appointments or admissions must not exceed 50%, except in extraordinary regional circumstances.
C) All reservations must expire automatically every five years unless renewed by plebiscite.
D) Reservations were permitted only in state legislatures and forbidden in public employment.
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court ruled that Article 16(4) must be balanced with equality under Article 16(1), mandating that overall reservations cannot exceed 50% except in rare, isolated areas.

questions.question: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog embodies cooperative federalism by including which institutional representatives?
options: A) Exclusively the Union Cabinet Ministers and Reserve Bank of India directors
B) The Chief Justices of all State High Courts and the Chief Justice of India
C) The Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all States, and Lieutenant Governors/Administrators of Union Territories
D) The Chairmen of all leading private corporate chambers (FICCI and CII)
questions.explanation: Unlike the National Development Council of the past, NITI Aayog's primary decision-making body is its Governing Council, comprising all State Chief Ministers and UT administrators.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The nuclear standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War was stabilized by the logic of 'Mutual Assured Destruction' (MAD), which posits that:
options: A) Neither superpower possessed functional nuclear warheads or ballistic missiles.
B) A conventional ground war could be fought indefinitely without any risk of escalation.
C) The United Nations could automatically disarm any nation launching an ICBM.
D) Both superpowers possessed sufficient invulnerable second-strike nuclear forces to completely annihilate the attacker, making the initiation of nuclear war suicidal.
questions.explanation: MAD rested on second-strike capability: even if one superpower launched a surprise first strike, the other retained enough submarine- and silo-based weapons to destroy the aggressor.

questions.question: Following the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, the political trajectory in several Central Asian republics (such as Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan) was characterized by:
options: A) The consolidation of authoritarian regimes where former communist party leaders extended their presidential tenures through referendums and suppressed political opposition.
B) The immediate establishment of thriving multi-party Westminster parliamentary democracies.
C) The voluntary transfer of sovereign governance to the European Union.
D) The abolition of all state security apparatuses and complete demilitarization.
questions.explanation: Presidents like Nursultan Nazarbayev (Kazakhstan), Islam Karimov (Uzbekistan), and Saparmurat Niyazov (Turkmenistan) concentrated power, curtailed civil liberties, and stayed in office for decades.

questions.question: In international political economy, Robert Keohane's 'Hegemonic Stability Theory' explains that while a hegemon creates international institutions (such as the WTO, IMF, and World Bank):
options: A) Institutions automatically self-destruct the instant the hegemon's GDP falls below 50% of the world total.
B) These international regimes can persist and maintain global order even as the hegemon's relative power declines, because states value stability and reduced transaction costs.
C) No state other than the hegemon ever derives any economic benefit from global trade rules.
D) International regimes are maintained entirely by military occupation of trade ports.
questions.explanation: In 'After Hegemony' (1984), Keohane argued that international institutions persist beyond hegemonic primacy because they provide valuable public goods, rules, and certainty.

questions.question: In 2005, the European Union's ambitious attempt to adopt a single formal 'Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe' was derailed when it was rejected in national referendums by voters in:
options: A) Germany and Italy
B) Spain and Portugal
C) France and the Netherlands
D) Poland and Hungary
questions.explanation: In May-June 2005, voters in France and the Netherlands decisively rejected the EU Constitution, forcing EU leaders to abandon a single constitution and draft the Lisbon Treaty instead.

questions.question: In November 1988, the Indian armed forces executed 'Operation Cactus' in the Maldives. What was the mission and outcome of this operation?
options: A) India annexed the southern atolls of the Maldives as an administrative union territory.
B) Indian forces conducted deep-water nuclear testing off the coast of Male.
C) The operation evacuated all foreign diplomats and dissolved the Maldivian parliament.
D) Indian paratroopers and naval warships swiftly thwarted a coup d'état attempted by Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries (PLOTE) against President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom.
questions.explanation: Upon request from President Gayoom, Indian paratroopers landed in Male within hours, captured mercenary invaders fleeing by ship, and restored the elected government with zero civilian casualties.

questions.question: During the 1956 Suez Crisis, UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld and Canadian diplomat Lester B. Pearson pioneered which novel international security instrument?
options: A) The first armed United Nations Emergency Force (UNEF I) to monitor troop withdrawal and buffer opposing armies
B) The first UN atomic bombing strike against the aggressor nations
C) The total economic boycott of all maritime vessels passing through the Mediterranean
D) The dissolution of the UN General Assembly during wartime
questions.explanation: Hammarskjöld and Pearson created UNEF I in 1956, inventing classic peacekeeping ('Chapter VI and a half') where neutral, lightly-armed blue helmets separate combatants with their consent.

questions.question: A fundamental difference between the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC, 1993) and the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC, 1972) lies in their verification mechanisms:
options: A) The BWC has strict satellite inspections while the CWC relies entirely on verbal trust.
B) The CWC is overseen by an independent verification body (OPCW) with mandatory challenge inspections, whereas the BWC lacks any multilateral verification protocol.
C) Neither convention has ever entered into legal force under international law.
D) Both conventions permit states to manufacture chemical and biological munitions for defensive retail.
questions.explanation: The CWC is supported by the OPCW in The Hague with rigorous on-site verification and challenge inspections, whereas the BWC never established an inspectorate or verification protocol.

questions.question: The 1997 Kyoto Protocol introduced three innovative market-based 'flexible mechanisms' to help Annex I countries meet their emissions targets cost-effectively. These are:
options: A) Carbon Penal Tax, Mandatory Deforestation Bans, and Industrial Shutdown Orders
B) Nuclear Power Transfers, Ocean Dumping Credits, and Solar Subsidies
C) Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), Joint Implementation (JI), and International Emissions Trading (IET)
D) Global Wealth Redistribution, Universal Tariffs, and Sovereign Debt Cancellation
questions.explanation: The Kyoto flexible mechanisms allowed developed nations to earn emission credits by investing in clean projects in developing nations (CDM), other Annex I countries (JI), or trading emissions (IET).

questions.question: Economist Dani Rodrik's famous 'Political Trilemma of the World Economy' asserts that it is impossible to simultaneously achieve all three of the following:
options: A) Low inflation, high interest rates, and high employment
B) Free speech, military conscription, and universal healthcare
C) Agricultural subsidies, urban industrialisation, and environmental purity
D) Hyperglobalisation, National Sovereignty (the nation-state), and Democratic Politics
questions.explanation: Rodrik's trilemma posits that societies can have at most two out of three: if you want deep economic globalisation and democracy, you must sacrifice national sovereignty (global governance); if you want national sovereignty and globalisation, you sacrifice democracy.

questions.question: The French colonial territories in India (Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam) were peacefully transferred to the Indian Union in de facto control in 1954, but de jure transfer was ratified by the French Parliament in:
options: A) 1962, followed by the 14th Constitutional Amendment Act
B) 1947, immediately upon Indian independence
C) 1950, when the Constitution came into force
D) 1975, alongside Sikkim's accession
questions.explanation: France and India signed a treaty of cession in 1956, ratified by the French Parliament in May 1962. Parliament then passed the 14th Amendment in 1962, creating the Union Territory of Pondicherry.

questions.question: To tackle the unprecedented logistical challenge of enrolling women voters in the 1951-52 elections, Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen took the firm democratic decision that:
options: A) Women were completely exempted from voting for the first decade of independence.
B) Women whose names were registered merely as 'wife of X' or 'daughter of Y' rather than by their own legal names were removed from rolls until properly re-enrolled.
C) Women were given special postal ballots that could be signed by their husbands.
D) All women were automatically assigned the names of ancient historical queens.
questions.explanation: When over 2.8 million women were listed without their own names (e.g. 'wife of...'), Sukumar Sen refused to accept such rolls, insisting on women's individual citizenship identity.

questions.question: The 'Gadgil Formula', adopted in 1969 by the National Development Council for the allocation of Central plan assistance to Indian states, assigned the highest weightage (60%) to which criterion?
options: A) Per capita income of the state
B) Tax effort of the state
C) Population of the state
D) Special development problems
questions.explanation: The Gadgil Formula allocated Central Plan assistance with 60% weight to population, 10% to per capita state domestic product, 10% to tax effort, and 20% to special problems.

questions.sub_topic: Line of Control in Simla Agreement
questions.question: Under the historic Simla Agreement signed on 2 July 1972 by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, the Ceasefire Line in Jammu and Kashmir resulting from the 1971 war was converted into the:
options: A) Permanent international boundary formally demarcated with border pillars
B) McMahon Line, monitored by United Nations observers
C) Radcliffe Line, overseen by the International Court of Justice
D) Line of Control (LoC), which both sides agreed to respect without prejudice to their recognized positions
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement converted the 1971 ceasefire line into the Line of Control (LoC), committing both countries to respect it bilaterally without seeking to alter it unilaterally.

questions.question: According to the findings of the Shah Commission of Inquiry, what unconstitutional irregularity occurred on the night of 25 June 1975 prior to the declaration of Emergency?
options: A) The Chief Election Commissioner dissolved the Supreme Court of India.
B) Prime Minister Indira Gandhi advised President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to declare the Emergency without consulting the Union Cabinet, which was informed only the following morning.
C) The Army Chief of Staff refused to obey civilian commands and seized the radio station.
D) The President refused to sign the proclamation until forced at gunpoint.
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission revealed that the Cabinet was bypassed; Indira Gandhi invoked emergency rules to advise the President unilaterally on 25 June, informing her Cabinet ministers only at a 6 AM meeting on 26 June.

questions.question: The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971, dramatically altered the political map of northeast India by conferring full statehood on which three territories?
options: A) Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, and Nagaland
B) Assam, Sikkim, and Bhutan
C) Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Mizoram
D) Meghalaya, Manipur, and Tripura
questions.explanation: The 1971 Act elevated Meghalaya (an autonomous sub-state within Assam), Manipur, and Tripura (both UTs) to full statehood in January 1972, while creating Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh as Union Territories.
